panels.title: Henry III and the barons
points: Civil war: the Battle of Lewes, 1264

parts.text: Point: to get taxes for wars
Evidence: Edward I called the 1295 Parliament during wars with France, Scotland and Wales
Explain: taxes paid more willingly when representatives agreed

keywords.def: a meeting of the king with nobles, churchmen and representatives

questions.q: Explain why the 1265 Parliament was different. (2 marks)
questions.a: It included knights and burgesses (1), so ordinary landholders and towns were represented for the first time (1)

questions.q: Who led the barons in the 1260s?
What did kings mainly want from Parliament?

Core: Complete the Parliament flow chart (money, wars, consent, representatives), then answer in the portal response box: 'Why did Parliament develop?' Starter: 'Parliament developed mainly because ...'
questions.a: Links between war, tax and consent with 1265 and 1295 as evidence

questions.q: Extend: Compare Parliament in 1295 with Parliament today: one similarity, one difference.
questions.a: Similar: agrees taxes; different: elected by all adults today, women included

questions.q: Stretch: Was money or ideas about rights more important? Explain.
questions.a: A justified view: mainly money, but Magna Carta ideas mattered
B) Town representatives. Burgesses represented towns; knights represented counties.

questions.q: Big question: why would a king share power?
questions.a: He needed money for wars, and taxes were easier to collect with the agreement of representatives
